text: 3. **The FlatBuffers-generated Swift types are stale — NOT STARTED, this is the big one.** `TypedHomeFeedDecoder.swift` decodes the home feed's typed sidecar using generated types `nmp_nip01_OpFeedSnapshot` / `nmp_nip01_TimelineEventCard` / `nmp_nip01_RootCard` (checked in at `apps/ios/Chirp/Bridge/Generated/OpFeedSnapshot.generated.swift`, `TimelineSnapshot.generated.swift`) and hardcodes `schemaId = "nmp.nip01.opfeed"` / `fileIdentifier = "NOFS"`. All of that is gone: the current pin's actual schema lives at `crates/nmp-note-feed/schema/op_feed.fbs` under `namespace nmp.note_feed;`, with `OP_FEED_SCHEMA_ID = "nmp.note_feed.opfeed"`, `OP_FEED_FILE_IDENTIFIER = "NNFS"`, `OP_FEED_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` (verified directly in the pinned checkout). The card type itself renamed `TimelineEventCard`→`NoteFeedItem` and changed fields (dropped `relation_counts`, added `hosted_group`). Fixing this means: regenerating the Swift FlatBuffers bindings from the new `.fbs` (I found `flatc` is available locally, haven't run it yet), which will produce a new `nmp_note_feed_*`-prefixed type family, then rewriting `TypedHomeFeedDecoder.swift`'s field-by-field mapping to match. This is a real, multi-file migration of comparable size to what I just finished for tui/desktop/android-ffi — not a quick follow-on to a key rename. [...] - chirp#35 — the cross-platform OP-feed-schema decode migration (`nmp.nip01.opfeed`/`NOFS`/`TimelineEventCard` v1 → `nmp.note_feed.opfeed`/`NNFS`/`NoteFeedItem` v2). Full per-platform inventory in the issue body.
